column2: On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) say: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest of faith.” Reported by Muslim.
Minkum (“among you”): you, the company of legally responsible Muslims.
Munkaran (“an evil”): something the Sharīʿah deems ugly, in deed or word, even if minor.
Fa-l-yughayyirhu (“let him change it”): let him remove it
bi-yadihi (“with his hand”): where it is something that can be removed by hand, such as breaking an instrument of idle entertainment or a vessel of wine.
“If he cannot”: object with his hand, because the one doing it is stronger than him and he would be harmed by changing it by hand,
“then with his tongue”: by words, such as a reminder or a rebuke.
“And if he cannot”: do that with his tongue because of some obstacle, such as fear of strife, fear for his life, or the like,
“then with his heart”: he must oppose it [inwardly], by hating it with his heart and resolving that if he were able to speak or act, he would speak and act.
Wa-dhālika (“and that”): opposing it with the heart,
“is the weakest of faith”: the least in fruit.

The obligation to change evil by every means one is able to of those mentioned; admonition is not sufficient for one who is able to remove it by hand, nor the heart for one who is able to remove it by tongue.

Opposing evil relates only to what is established with certainty. The one who enjoins good and forbids evil may not storm into houses on the basis of suspicion, unless someone whose word he trusts informs him
that a man has taken another man aside to kill him, or a woman to commit fornication with her, or something similar that cannot be undone; then he must investigate, for fear of its being missed.
Whoever is able to do a quality of faith and does it is better than one who leaves it out of inability, as is also shown by his ﷺ saying about women:

“As for the deficiency in her religion, she spends days and nights without praying.” This shows that whoever is able to do the obligation and does it is more deserving and better than one who leaves it out of inability or with an excuse.

Not opposing evil even with the heart is evidence that faith has gone from him. That is why Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “Ruined is he who does not know good and evil with his heart.”
